records.title: THE ODYSSEY

linkouts.label: The reconstruction · Danek & Hagel, via Open Culture

card: Sung, in meter, to an instrument, by a performer who could not read. The pronunciation here is a reconstruction (the vowels are scholarship, the pitch is argument) but the meter is not: it survives in the lines themselves.
What plays is a modern scholar doing what the first singers did: composing sound, not consulting a page. No translation appears. These words were made for the ear, not the eye.

records.title: THE ODYSSEY

linkouts.label: Center for Hellenic Studies · Avdo Međedović, Guslar

card: Avdo Međedović could not read or write. In 1935, in Bijelo Polje, he sang for Milman Parry's aluminum discs: epics the length of the Odyssey, improvised in formulas held in the body, never twice the same. Parry recorded him to prove Homer had worked the same way.
Composition and performance were one act. Beneath a given performance there was no original to consult; there was only the next performance.

records.title: THE ODYSSEY
card: The same opening lines, six ways, 1616 to 2017. Homer's first adjective for his man, polytropos, has never settled in English; each era's answer sits beneath the frame.
Every version replaces the last, and the frame never moves.

extra.greekLine1: ἄνδρα μοι ἔννεπε, μοῦσα, πολύτροπον, ὃς μάλα πολλὰ…

translations.polytropos: many a way / wound with his wisdom
translations.text:
The man, O Muse, inform, that many a way
Wound with his wisdom to his wished stay;
That wander'd wondrous far, when he the town
Of sacred Troy had sack'd and shiver'd down;
The cities of a world of nations,
With all their manners, minds, and fashions,
He saw and knew; at sea felt many woes,
Much care sustain'd, to save from overthrows
Himself and friends in their retreat for home.

The man for wisdom's various arts renown'd,
Long exercised in woes, O Muse! resound;
Who, when his arms had wrought the destined fall
Of sacred Troy, and razed her heaven-built wall,
Wandering from clime to clime, observant stray'd,
Their manners noted, and their states survey'd,
On stormy seas unnumber'd toils he bore,
Safe with his friends to gain his natal shore.

translations.polytropos: skilled in all ways of contending
translations.text:
Sing in me, Muse, and through me tell the story
of that man skilled in all ways of contending…

linkout.label: The rest · Farrar, Straus and Giroux

translations.text: Tell me, Muse, of the man of many ways, who was driven…

translations.polytropos: the man of twists and turns
translations.text:
Sing to me of the man, Muse, the man of twists and turns
driven time and again off course…

Tell me about a complicated man.
Muse, tell me how he wandered and was lost…

In English, read by Sean Connery

card: Published in 1911, in Alexandria, in Greek. The poem holds that the destination's whole value is the traveling it produced; arrival is what the years of arriving were for.
The famous English versions came later. They differ from each other, and they are also versions.

extra.greekPoem:
Σα βγεις στον πηγαιμό για την Ιθάκη,
να εύχεσαι νάναι μακρύς ο δρόμος,
γεμάτος περιπέτειες, γεμάτος γνώσεις.
Τους Λαιστρυγόνας και τους Κύκλωπας,
τον θυμωμένο Ποσειδώνα μη φοβάσαι,
τέτοια στον δρόμο σου ποτέ σου δεν θα βρείς,
αν μέν' η σκέψις σου υψηλή, αν εκλεκτή
συγκίνησις το πνεύμα και το σώμα σου αγγίζει.
Τους Λαιστρυγόνας και τους Κύκλωπας,
τον άγριο Ποσειδώνα δεν θα συναντήσεις,
αν δεν τους κουβανείς μες στην ψυχή σου,
αν η ψυχή σου δεν τους στήνει εμπρός σου.

Να εύχεσαι νάναι μακρύς ο δρόμος.
Πολλά τα καλοκαιρινά πρωϊά να είναι
που με τι ευχαρίστησι, με τι χαρά
θα μπαίνεις σε λιμένας πρωτοειδωμένους·
να σταματήσεις σ' εμπορεία Φοινικικά,
και τες καλές πραγμάτειες ν' αποκτήσεις,
σεντέφια και κοράλλια, κεχριμπάρια κ' έβενους,
και ηδονικά μυρωδικά κάθε λογής,
όσο μπορείς πιο άφθονα ηδονικά μυρωδικά·
σε πόλεις Aιγυπτιακές πολλές να πας,
να μάθεις και να μάθεις απ' τους σπουδασμένους.

Πάντα στον νου σου νάχεις την Ιθάκη.
Το φθάσιμον εκεί είν' ο προορισμός σου.
Aλλά μη βιάζεις το ταξείδι διόλου.
Καλλίτερα χρόνια πολλά να διαρκέσει·
και γέρος πια ν' αράξεις στο νησί,
πλούσιος με όσα κέρδισες στον δρόμο,
μη προσδοκώντας πλούτη να σε δώσει η Ιθάκη.

Η Ιθάκη σ' έδωσε τ' ωραίο ταξείδι.
Χωρίς αυτήν δεν θάβγαινες στον δρόμο.
Άλλα δεν έχει να σε δώσει πια.

Κι αν πτωχική την βρεις, η Ιθάκη δεν σε γέλασε.
Έτσι σοφός που έγινες, με τόση πείρα,
ήδη θα το κατάλαβες η Ιθάκες τι σημαίνουν.

records.title: THE ODYSSEY
card: 1| Greek epic runs on two values in tension: nostos, the homecoming, and kleos, the fame that outlives the singer. Heroes generally choose one.
2| She left the Smoky Mountains at eighteen and spent sixty years singing her way back, to a cabin rebuilt full scale inside her own theme park. A homecoming to a reconstruction.
3| She wrote 'I Will Always Love You' as a farewell; another singer's performance permanently eclipsed it. Same song, second voice, larger. Every record in this jukebox is that.

4| Appalachian balladry is an oral tradition: Scots-Irish songs carried across water and mutated for three centuries by people who did not write them down. She was raised inside it. Play A2 again afterward.

5| She arranged, years ahead, for her death to be announced in another voice, on a recording she commissioned. She scripted her own transmission. Kleos and nostos, both; the whole reason this record is here.

media.videoLabel: Jason and the Argonauts · the skeleton sequence

card: Three years of one man's life, animated a frame at a time: seven skeletons moved by hand, joint by joint, until they fought.

Nolan has said he was looking for a gap in cinematic culture (mythological work never attempted at modern scale and weight) and has named this sequence among the reasons the 2026 film exists. The gap this record opened is the one the sealed record below was made to fill.

records.title: THE ODYSSEY
card: The first narrative feature shot start to finish on IMAX film cameras: over two million feet of film, ninety-one shooting days, much of it on open water. The camera was too loud to record dialogue beside, so a new blimp was built to quiet it, which put a large box between the actors, who found each other's eyes in mirrors placed around the lens.
The screenplay works from Emily Wilson's translation, the 2017 voice in B1. For reference, Nolan and van Hoytema screened Andrei Rublev and Ran.
The seal stays on until the theater.
